passage.title: Cutty Sark: the fastest sailing ship of its time

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text for Cutty Sark. The passage covers the history of the clipper ship Cutty Sark: named after a character in Robert Burns' poem 'Tam o' Shanter'; built under a contract that favoured John Willis; intended to be the fastest tea clipper on the UK–China route; lost its rudder in a storm racing Thermopylae; the Suez Canal made steam ships faster on the China route; Captain Woodget commanded it carrying wool from Australia via Antarctica; sold to Portuguese owners (renamed Ferreira); repaired at Falmouth after a storm; used for training from 1923–1954; twice damaged by fire in the 21st century.]

passage.title: Book Review: The Happiness Industry by William Davies

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text for Book Review: The Happiness Industry by William Davies. The passage is a review discussing Jeremy Bentham's influence on positive psychology and happiness research. It covers Bentham's utilitarian philosophy, his inventions including the Panopticon prison design, his ideas on measuring happiness, and his influence on modern psychology and behaviourism through John Watson. The reviewer discusses how the book explores the relationship between psychology and economics/industry.]
